intro.description: This cheat sheet guides you through the Platform Status Cleanup. The native cleanup uses a concise factory when equivalence is proven and otherwise retains the explicit identity in a shorter constructor. It never asks you to approve an unproven semantic change in the preview.

item.title: Understand the Two Safe Targets
item.description:
When a five-argument Status has a code that is provably IStatus.OK, the cleanup chooses one of two targets.
Proven bundle identity
new Status(IStatus.ERROR, PLUGIN_ID, IStatus.OK, message, exception)
→ Status.error(message, exception)
This factory form is used only when PLUGIN_ID is a side-effect-free compile-time String equal to the project Bundle-SymbolicName, or the identity is the exact enclosing class literal, and the factory return type fits the source context.
Identity not fully proven
new Status(IStatus.ERROR, responsiblePluginId, IStatus.OK, message, exception)
→ new Status(IStatus.ERROR, responsiblePluginId, message, exception)

item.title: Enable the Cleanup
item.description:
Open the Clean Up dialog:
1. Select an Eclipse plug-in project in Package Explorer
2. Choose Source → Clean Up…
3. Select Use custom profile and click Configure…
4. On Platform Status (Sandbox), enable the cleanup
5. Click OK
Click Perform to open the Source menu.

item.title: Know What Counts as a Proof
item.description:
The factory path requires project bundle metadata and a side-effect-free identity. A compile-time String matching Bundle-SymbolicName and the exact enclosing class literal are supported.
A method call such as JavaPlugin.getPluginId() remains in the constructor fallback. Removing the method call or triggering its declaring class differently could be observable even when the returned String is expected to match.

item.title: Review the Real Execution Preview
Understand MultiStatus Handling
item.description:
MultiStatus may carry an application-specific code. The cleanup changes only a value that is provably zero:
new MultiStatus(pluginId, 0, message, exception)
→ new MultiStatus(pluginId, IStatus.OK, message, exception)
A nonzero constant, method call, or unresolved expression is left unchanged.
